patterns_noted: Critical lesson from today: ALWAYS check whether an analyst price target is above or below the current market price before treating it as a bullish catalyst. JPM raising GS target to $900 while GS trades at $1,055 is a Neutral/bearish signal, not a bull catalyst — the bull agent missed this entirely and I nearly executed on it. Second lesson: correlated single-day moves in a sector cohort driven by one Benzinga headline (DHT/FRO/TNK all up on same article) is NOT independent confirmation of a thesis — it is one trade repeated in three tickers. The Bear's INSW divergence point (-1.2% despite being in the same article) is the canary. Third lesson: micro-cap buyback announcements at sub-$5 prices warrant extreme skepticism — the math rarely works and the promotional pattern is well-established. Fourth: holding cash is the correct call when the highest-conviction available trade is 0.60-0.65 with material bear rebuttals. Deploying capital into marginal ideas to 'do something' consistently generates underperformance. The Momentum Growth portfolio beating me at +5.65% suggests I should weight technical momentum more heavily — look for names with clean 30d uptrends AND a near-term catalyst, not just one or the other.
